[USER] The user is looking for a new cherry recipe to try out.  
[PREFERENCE] The user is interested in cherry clafoutis or cherry crisp.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Cherry Clafoutis Recipe: Serves 6-8 people, ingredients include 2 cups fresh or frozen cherries, 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 teaspoon baking powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/2 cup whole milk, 2 large eggs, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Instructions for Cherry Clafoutis: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C), whisk together sugar, flour, and baking powder; whisk together milk, eggs, and melted butter; combine wet and dry ingredients; pour into baking dish, arrange cherries on top; bake for 35-40 minutes; dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Cherry Crisp Recipe: Serves 6-8 people, ingredients include 2 cups fresh or frozen cherries, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 2 tablespoons cornstarch, 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon salt, 1/2 cup rolled oats, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Instructions for Cherry Crisp: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C), mix cherries, granulated sugar, cornstarch, and flour; transfer to baking dish; mix rolled oats, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt; add cold butter to oat mixture; spread topping over cherry mixture; bake for 40-45 minutes; serve warm with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.  
[USER] The user is interested in trying the cherry clafoutis recipe but wants to substitute granulated sugar with brown sugar.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Brown sugar can be substituted for granulated sugar in the cherry clafoutis recipe, affecting flavor and texture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Flavor: Brown sugar gives a richer, deeper flavor with notes of caramel and molasses.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Texture: Brown sugar contains more moisture, resulting in a denser and more moist clafoutis that may not puff up as much.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for using brown sugar: Use light brown sugar, reduce to 1 1/4 cups, and cover with foil if over-browning occurs.
